text.title: Quality Gates Core Rules
text.summary: 11 testable rules: the six rows of the stack-to-gate matrix (which kind of test must exist for which kind of change), applicability computed from the git diff, two-layer enforcement in readiness.md and CI, framework neutrality, and API tests living with the code. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Backend only → unit tests REQUIRED + API tests REQUIRED. No Playwright. No UI audit.
rule.rationale: The matrix maps which test gates are mandatory based on what the feature actually touches; a backend-only change has no user-facing surface to drive.

rule.statement: Backend + Frontend (full-stack feature) → unit tests REQUIRED + API tests REQUIRED + Playwright happy path REQUIRED. UI audit REQUIRED if any visible UI changed.
rule.rationale: Both layers moved, so both layers' gates apply, plus the path that crosses them.

rule.statement: User-facing flow (any surface where the user takes ordered actions) → Playwright positive AND negative cases REQUIRED per flow. UI audit REQUIRED if web/mobile/TUI.
rule.rationale: Ordered user actions are where regressions are visible to customers; the negative case is what proves the flow fails safely.

rule.statement: Frontend only (no backend changes) → unit tests REQUIRED + Playwright pos+neg per flow REQUIRED. No API tests for this feature.
rule.rationale: No API contract moved, so an API gate would test nothing this feature changed.

rule.statement: Pure data (migration, ETL, no UI / API contract change) → unit tests REQUIRED + migration tests REQUIRED + reversibility check REQUIRED. No Playwright. No UI audit. No API tests.
rule.rationale: The risk in a data change is irreversibility, not user flow; the gates follow the risk.

rule.statement: Infrastructure / CI / build-system → unit tests on any logic changed + smoke check that build / deploy still produces a working artefact.
rule.rationale: A build-system change has no feature surface; what can break is the artefact itself.

rule.statement: Applicability is computed from the git diff, NOT from the developer's self-assessment of scope.
rule.rationale: Authors systematically underestimate which layers their change touches. The diff is the source of truth; the matrix is mechanical.

rule.statement: readiness.md MUST contain a tick (with evidence link) for every required gate from the matrix, OR a "n/a + one-line reason" when the matrix says the gate does not apply.
rule.rationale: The human-review layer catches "the tests passed but the assertion is empty" failures that CI cannot see.

rule.statement: CI MUST actually RUN every required gate and fail the build on a non-pass result. A green CI is mandatory before the feature moves to done/.
rule.rationale: The CI layer catches "the developer skipped the test locally" failures that human review cannot see at speed. Both layers are required; one without the other lets bugs through.

rule.statement: The methodology MUST NOT block a feature solely because a different framework was chosen for the same gate.
rule.rationale: The gate is "tests exist and pass". Framework politics is a separate decision recorded in project-spec/decisions/.

rule.statement: API tests must live with the code and run in CI.
rule.rationale: Postman collections do not run in CI without extra plumbing; they drift from the codebase.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit a gate-applicability record passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold.

rule.statement: Skip; throwaway prototype or pure-documentation project — no readiness-checklist, no CI, no user-facing or API surface to gate.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
